name: Tarragona
title: Tarragona Ship Thickness Gauging | Chemical Tankers & Bulkers
description: UTM at the Port of Tarragona for chemical, product and gas tankers, grain and bulk carriers: ultrasonic thickness gauging of hull, tanks and piping.
h1: Tarragona Ultrasonic Thickness Surveys: Liquid Bulk and Dry Bulk Ships
intro: The Port of Tarragona is the main liquid bulk harbour of Catalonia, serving a large petrochemical cluster, and it also handles grain, fertiliser and other dry bulk. Chemical and product tankers dominate the berths, which means permit rules, tank cleaning and cargo sequences shape every survey. Our ultrasonic thickness team travels from India to the ship, with access arranged by the agent, and plans readings of ballast tanks, decks, holds and piping to suit the terminal.

highlights.p: Chemical tankers wear in ballast tanks, deck lines and cargo piping brackets. We read plating and structure in spaces the crew has made safe, so wastage is shown on a thickness plan well before the renewal survey.

Liquid bulk berths have their own permits, hot-work limits and entry procedures. Scope and sequence are agreed with the superintendent and the terminal through the agent before the technicians fly, so no hours are lost on arrival.
Dry bulk quays give open access to holds once a cargo has gone. Frames, hopper plating, coamings and deck lines are read between cargoes, helping owners plan steel renewal before their next docking.

port.h: The Port of Tarragona: Catalonia's liquid bulk gateway
p: The Port de Tarragona lies on the Costa Daurada, south-west of Barcelona, with the old Roman city rising above its seafront. The harbour is protected by long breakwaters and has been extended over the decades to accommodate large tankers and bulk ships. The approach is straightforward from the open Mediterranean, and pilots board outside the entrance. The berths are organised by cargo: chemical and oil products on the main liquid quays, solid bulk on separate wharves, and a smaller area for general cargo, ro-ro and cruise ships.

The surrounding petrochemical complex is the port's engine. A refinery and a cluster of chemical plants receive crude, feedstocks and gases, and send out finished products, so tankers of many sizes use the liquid bulk berths. Chemical tankers carrying parcels of different grades call regularly, along with product and LPG carriers, and bunkering and small coastal tankers move around the basin. On the dry side, grain, animal feed ingredients, fertiliser and other bulk cargoes arrive for the agricultural hinterland of Catalonia and Aragón. Container and ro-ro activity are minor, and cruise visits are occasional.

Because tanker work revolves around cargo programmes, stays are usually short, ranging from a day to two or three, with waiting periods at the anchorage when berths are busy. The tide range is small, so berth depth stays steady, and weather is the main variable: eastern and south-eastern gales can disrupt anchorage work and slow port operations, while summer provides calmer conditions for launches. Tank cleaning and gas-freeing are frequent for chemical ships, which suits thickness work in ballast and slop spaces. A visit can often combine a tanker at a liquid berth with a bulk carrier on a neighbouring wharf, since the quays are close together.

facilities.h: Where UTM takes place in Tarragona
p: Most gauging is done alongside at the liquid bulk berths, where chemical, product and gas tankers lie for discharge or loading. The terminal's safety rules decide who may board, what equipment can be used and which spaces may be opened, and the ship's enclosed-space entry system covers the technicians. Ballast tanks, voids, cofferdams, the shell above the waterline and deck piping are normal subjects during cargo work; cargo tanks need cleaning and gas-freeing first, so they are handled when the ship has finished its programme.

The dry bulk quays are less restricted. Ships there discharge grain or fertiliser and then wait for the next cargo, which opens holds for readings of frames, hopper plating, bulkheads and hatch coamings. The port does not have a drydock for ocean-going merchant ships, so ships needing renewal normally dock at Barcelona, Valencia or a yard further afield; Tarragona is the right place to measure wastage and plan the work. Repair firms in the port can handle afloat work such as piping renewal, and gauging can be matched with their schedules. Anchorage jobs are possible for short checks, subject to launch availability and sea state.
list: Chemical and oil product berths — ballast tank, void, cofferdam and deck piping readings under terminal permit rules
LPG and gas berths — hull, ballast tank and deck readings, without cargo containment, within terminal procedures
Dry bulk wharves for grain and fertiliser — hold frame, hopper, coaming and deck gauging between cargoes
General cargo and ro-ro berths — hull and tween deck readings on coasters and short-sea ships
Tarragona anchorage — short sampling jobs on tankers and bulkers waiting for a berth, weather permitting
Docking yards at Barcelona and Valencia — gauging begun here continues beside the docking survey

context.h: Port state control, ESP and chemical trade rules
p: Port state control at Tarragona operates under the Paris MoU and is carried out by the Capitanía Marítima, part of Spain's Dirección General de la Marina Mercante. Chemical and gas tankers are under particular attention, and inspectors often look at the condition of ballast tanks, deck structure and piping when a ship has been trading for years without a docking. For ships under the Enhanced Survey Programme, thickness records are the thread connecting one renewal survey to the next, and they show where substantial corrosion is developing.

Industry and regulation meet in this port. Chemical charterers and terminal operators often ask for evidence of condition before fixing a ship, and some vetting systems look closely at structural records. Under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, ships calling at EU ports need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime influence voyage planning. Owners of stainless-steel chemical tankers face different concerns from those of coated carbon steel ships, and we gauge both with attention to the coating and the corrosion pattern, but we do not inspect the coatings themselves.

jobs.h: Typical gauging jobs at the Port of Tarragona
jobs.p: Most jobs in Tarragona start with a tanker, a terminal and a permit. Scope, access and report layout are agreed with the superintendent while the technicians are still in India, so berth hours go on measurement. Dry bulk ships bring a different pattern, with more open access and a timetable based on loading. Examples of work that fits this port:
list: Ballast tank and deck gauging on a chemical tanker ahead of its renewal survey, with a thickness plan for steel renewal.
Void and cofferdam readings on a product tanker discharging at a liquid berth, within terminal permits.
Hold frame, hopper plating and coaming gauging on a bulk carrier after discharging grain.
Piping and bracket readings on a gas carrier or LPG ship, compared with earlier gauging.
Pre-purchase or charterer's condition gauging on a short-sea tanker calling at the port.

logistics: Reus Airport lies close to Tarragona and has seasonal European links, but technicians travelling from India more often reach Barcelona-El Prat through a European or Gulf hub and continue to the port by road or rail. The ship's agent arranges terminal passes and a launch for anchorage work. Schengen visas are required, so please send the ship's expected dates early; once visas are issued we confirm mobilisation, since tanker schedules can change with cargo programmes.

faqs.q: Can a chemical tanker be gauged during cargo operations at Tarragona?
faqs.a: Yes, in spaces the ship has made safe. Ballast tanks, voids, cofferdams, the shell and deck piping can be read while cargo moves, within terminal rules and the ship's entry system. Cargo tanks need cleaning and gas-freeing, so they are better left to a period when the ship is out of service.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Tarragona for large ships?
faqs.a: No drydock for ocean-going merchant ships. Repair firms do afloat work, but ships needing steel renewal usually dock at Barcelona, Valencia or elsewhere. Gauging at Tarragona gives you measured wastage figures to take to the yard, so quotations can be compared on the same data.

faqs.q: What access do bulkers offer after grain discharge?
faqs.a: Once a hold is empty and swept, frames, hopper plating, bulkheads and coamings can be read. Dust and residue can slow access, so the chief officer's preparation matters. We agree the hold order with the agent and stop when the next cargo operation begins.

faqs.q: Do you take readings on stainless steel chemical tankers?
faqs.a: Yes. We measure wall thickness on stainless and carbon steel with suitable probes and calibration blocks, and we report the results by space. Coating condition and cargo tank surfaces are outside our scope, but plating, deck structure and piping can be measured, and the report follows the usual thickness measurement layout.

faqs.q: Can ships at the anchorage be gauged?
faqs.a: Short sampling jobs are possible when a launch is arranged and the sea state allows. Tankers waiting for a berth can give some hours, though they may move at short notice. A narrow list of spaces is more practical than a full survey, and a berth stop is better for anything larger.
